headline: ML feature selection nominates candidate biomarkers from public transcriptomic cohorts
label: Machine Learning Biomarker Discovery
summary: Public transcriptomic and single-cell datasets are routinely mined with LASSO, SVM-RFE and related learners to nominate diagnostic hub genes, now with…
synthesis: The dominant thread is a bioinformatics pipeline applied to public transcriptomic cohorts, in which differential expression or WGCNA modules are intersected with machine learning feature selection (LASSO, random forest, SVM-RFE, Boruta, Elastic Net, SHAP) to nominate diagnostic or prognostic hub genes. Examples span glioblastoma platelet RNA, mesothelioma, sepsis, allergic rhinitis, Kawasaki disease, diabetic retinopathy and gestational diabetes. Several add immune profiling or single-cell communication analysis, as with PLXNB2 in diabetic retinopathy, and SORT1 in septic shock is tested by in silico knockout. The contribution of most items is incremental, a consistent workflow applied to new disease contexts. The preprint IQC differs in scope, proposing an entropy-based ensemble metric that quantifies elastic net feature-selection stability in high-dimensional biological data, validated by simulation.
